introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné de 3 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 4, questions 5 et 6), lu en image ; aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food And Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » ; les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Pour 2(a), 5(a) et 6(b), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties (i) et (ii) imprimées (2+5, 2+5, 3+5).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au nombre exact d'éléments demandés. D'autres réponses sont valables pour les questions de liste ; le barème d'un point par élément est une hypothèse (le sujet ne le détaille pas). Aucune teneur nutritive chiffrée n'est avancée, sauf l'énergie d'un gramme de lipide (environ 37 kJ, valeur du programme).

Question 1(e) « mechanical raising agents » : le programme n'en nomme usuellement que deux (l'air et la vapeur), le sujet en demande quatre. Le corrigé donne quatre procédés mécaniques distincts (air par tamisage, par crémage, par fouettage, et vapeur) ; d'autres manuels répondent autrement (battage, pliage, laminage). À relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition.

Faits de cours à relire par un enseignant : les objectifs alimentaires de 5(b) (le sujet n'en impose aucun), les causes de faible production de 5(c) et les points de 6(d) sont des listes de manuel ; plusieurs autres réponses seraient acceptées.

Fautes d'impression du sujet recopiées telles quelles : « five (5) importance » au singulier (1d, 2a ii, 2d, 4d), « (5marks) », « (8marks) », « Recall three (3) advantages », « Pick out three (3) advantages ... of microwave cooking » sans point final, « Outline three (3) advantages and two (2) disadvantages of boiling » sans point final, « Define invitation ».

questions.corrige_markdown: **Food additives** are substances that are added to food in small quantities, during its preparation or processing, to preserve it or to improve its appearance (colour), flavour, texture or nutritive value. They are not usually eaten as food on their own (examples: preservatives, colourings, flavourings, sweeteners, emulsifiers).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give three (3) advantages and two (2) disadvantages of food additives.

(5marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Advantages (3 marks).**

1. **They preserve food and make it last longer** (preservatives prevent the growth of moulds and bacteria), so there is less waste.
2. **They improve the colour, flavour and texture of food**, so it looks and tastes more attractive (colourings, flavourings, sweeteners).
3. **They can add nutritive value** (for example iodine added to salt, vitamins added to flour or margarine) and keep a mixture smooth and stable (emulsifiers).

**Disadvantages (2 marks).**

1. **Some people are allergic** to some additives (colourings, preservatives), and some additives are suspected to be harmful when taken in large quantities over a long time.
2. **They can be used to hide poor quality or stale food** (for example colours and flavours that make old food look and taste fresh), and they may reduce the natural flavour of the food.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Enumerate five (5) functions of water in the body.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five functions of water in the body (1 mark each):

1. **It is a solvent** in which nutrients and other substances dissolve, and the medium in which chemical reactions of the body take place.
2. **It transports** digested food, oxygen and hormones to the cells and carries waste products away (blood is mostly water).
3. **It regulates body temperature**: sweat evaporates from the skin and cools the body.
4. **It helps digestion**, since saliva and the digestive juices contain a large amount of water, and it softens the food and prevents constipation.
5. **It removes waste products** from the body in urine and sweat, and it keeps joints and tissues moist and lubricated.
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write down five (5) uses of wood in the kitchen.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five uses of wood in the kitchen (1 mark each):

1. **Chopping (cutting) boards** and bread boards - wood does not blunt the knife.
2. **Wooden spoons and spatulas** for stirring and mixing food - they do not conduct heat, so they do not burn the hand.
3. **Rolling pins** for rolling out pastry and dough.
4. **Fuel (firewood)** for cooking in a wood fire or wood-burning stove.
5. **Kitchen furniture and fittings** - tables, shelves, cupboards, stools - and the handles of knives, saucepans and utensils.

(Other correct points: mortar and pestle, salad bowls and trays.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline and explain four (4) uses of milk in the diet.

(8marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four uses of milk in the diet (1 mark for the use and 1 mark for the explanation, so 2 marks each):

1. **It builds strong bones and teeth.** Milk is a good source of calcium (with phosphorus and some vitamin D), which is needed for the growth of bones and teeth; it is therefore very important for children, pregnant women and nursing mothers.
2. **It supplies protein for growth and repair.** Milk protein is of high biological value (it contains all the essential amino acids), so milk helps young children to grow and repairs worn-out tissues.
3. **It supplies energy and vitamins.** Milk contains lactose (milk sugar) and fat, which give energy, and vitamins A and B (riboflavin), which keep the skin, eyes and nerves healthy.
4. **It is used in cooking and to make other foods.** Milk is used in tea and coffee, porridge, sauces, custards, puddings, cakes and baby food, and it is made into butter, cheese and yoghurt, which makes the diet more varied.
